summary: Piscataquis Co., ME: first tower 1905, metal replacement 1919; cab moved to Greenville in 2011 or 2012 and still stands there per a 2024 report; summit tower gone.

facts.design: Steel tower with wooden cab (NHLR); the first tower was wooden and a metal tower replaced it in 1919 (WABI)
facts.status_note: Summit tower gone; the cab was moved to Greenville, where it stands (WABI, 2024)

staffing.status: no longer staffed; watch ended 1968 or 1976 depending on source

access.note: Cab stands at the Moosehead Lake Region Visitors Center in Greenville (WABI, 2024). The 2011 plan was to open a rebuilt lookout to the public; no current hours or opening notice found

events.note: First tower built by the M.G. Shaw Lumber Co. (NHLR); WABI also gives 1905
Original wooden tower placed in operation June 10, 1905; William Hilton of Greenville first watchman (Maine Memory)
Metal tower replaced the original wooden structure
NHLR gives 1959 for the present steel tower with wooden cab; conflicts with 1919
Closed for good and replaced by aircraft patrols, per Maine Memory
Fire watchmen maintained a constant presence until 1976, per WABI
Tower airlifted from the summit and cab moved to Greenville, October 11, 2011 per Forest Lookouts; WABI says 2011
Maine Memory dates the relocation to the Natural Resource Education Center in October 2012

corrections.current: 1919 built ('Built' field on NHLR detail page)
corrections.proposed: 1905 built (first tower); a metal tower replaced it in 1919
corrections.why: The NHLR page's own description says the first tower was built in 1905, and WABI gives 1905 for the first tower and 1919 for the metal replacement. The 1919 'Built' field matches the replacement, not the first tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR's Built field says 1919, but its text says the first tower was built in 1905 and the present steel tower with wooden cab in 1959. WABI says 1905 for the first tower and 1919 for the metal replacement. Forest Lookouts quotes a 1919 report for a 12-foot steel tower.
WABI says watchmen kept a constant presence until 1976. Maine Memory says the tower was closed for good in 1968. The story gives both.
Forest Lookouts and WABI put the removal of the tower or cab in 2011. Maine Memory dates the relocation to October 2012.

Forest Lookouts and Maine Memory name the Natural Resources or Resource Education Center in Greenville; WABI names the Moosehead Lake Region Visitors Center. The brief's name, Greenville Visitor Center, appears in none of the sources read.

notes_for_editor: The brief's NHLR slug for the relocated site (squaw-mountain-at-greenville-visitor-center) returned 404 in the cache and live, so it is not cited. The height of 3.7 m comes from Forest Lookouts' '12-foot' figure, which may describe a different structure or the cab; NHLR gives no height. Build, closure and relocation dates conflict across sources and are shown as conflicts, not settled. Access to the summit is not confirmed. The brief's 'Greenville Visitor Center' name is not used because no source read says it.
